external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Wellington LP286 from 12 OTU crashing at Edgcote Park on 18 April 1945. The aircraft suffered starboard engine problems during a cross-country navigation exercise and stalled after an overshoot attempt, crashing at 14:03. Five of six crew killed.

memorial_details:
Name: Vickers Wellington LP286
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Dedicatory engraved metal plaque attached to a freestanding stone post. At centre top of plaque is a blackened side view line drawing of a Wellington bomber below which, an inscription and basic details of the affected air crew.
Inscription: " Prepare For Battle " / WELLINGTON BOMBER LP286 OF No 12 O.T.U. / R.A.F. CHIPPING WARDEN CRASHED HERE AT / 1403 HRS 18 APRIL 1945 / (5 NAMES) / PERISHED / (1 NAME) / SURVIVED
Location: What3Words ref. - panoramic.nerd.lanes Wellington Bomber LP286 Air Crew Memorial Edgecote House Drive off Mill Lane Chipping Warden South Northamptonshire Northamptonshire OX17 1JX England
Grid Ref: SP 50082 48536
Coordinates: 52.132867310559,-1.269728656072
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/119/286/large_20210728_195819_0.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/119/287/large_20210728_195709.jpg
narrative:
After suffering starboard engine problems the pilot returned to base. The pilot failed to land on the first attempt and went around. At 14.03 hrs the aircraft clipped trees coming down south east of the airfield and caught fire. The only survivor being the rear gunner. Nigel Harris continues:
